content.label: I am a  physician retired after >50 years in practice. I rely on Medisafe personally and highly recommend it to others.

title.label: Title: Essential for Family Caregiving – Needs a "Multi-Caregiver Signature" Feature

content.label:
Medisafe is an excellent app for medication management, but it could be a game-changer for families who share the responsibility of caring for elderly parents.
Currently, when multiple family members (caregivers) are linked to one patient profile as 'Medfriends,' it is difficult to track exactly who administered a dose. We often face confusion or duplicate questions in our family chats.
I strongly suggest adding a 'Multi-Caregiver Signature' or 'Team Logging' feature. The app should explicitly record and display the specific name of the member who confirmed each dose. This would ensure clear accountability, seamless coordination, and much-needed peace of mind for family teams. Thank you for a great tool!"

I’m about ready to uninstall this app.   It has so much bloat of unnecessary stuff. 
And lately, every time I open it, it is on a tab with stuff about HIV meds which I don’t take,  and not my pill box.   

I already switched my partner to a different, simple app. I wanted to keep mine on this so I could identify the different ring tones. My pills increased after being in the hospital. I couldn’t keep up with all the different times I had to take them. This app is wonderful. Easy to use and setup. A lifesaver for me.

Pro: If you’re seeking app to help you remember to take medication and to ensure there’s no interactions, this is a fantastic app with reminders and critical alerts. It tries hard to make sure you don’t forget.

Con: It has an ability to connect accounts with a friend and is supposed to notify them if you don’t take meds. It does do this, but it also notifies the friend even if you did take meds and marked it in the system timely.

It’s done this to me several times where I’ve taken 8 o’clock pills at 8, marked it in the app, and by 9 it’s telling me it notified my friend that I didn’t take pills.

Subscription required from Jan 1 2026 onwards? Ridiculous. You already have a paid tier. That you haven't put out good enough paid features is your issue, and we should not be made to pay for those people's ineptitude.

Seriously, there's so few features in paid that I can't imagine how someone would willingly pay. I would *like* to have some alternative alarms, but nothing there is remotely better unless you have very special tastes and never have others around when your alarms ring. Nor do you get better data retention, better report options, more flexible reminder options, better home screen designs, etc.

I’ve been using this app for a long time, and now the developers have decided to introduce a subscription model. Some time ago, they already removed features that had always been available. While this is probably legal, it feels untrustworthy. Now they are removing almost everything unless you pay for a subscription.

Most apps don’t take away existing features; they usually add new options that users can choose to purchase.

I’ve been critical in the past and shared feedback—especially about how the app handles crossing time zones—but nothing meaningful ever changed. The developers clearly don’t understand how meditation should work when travelling across time zones, and the result is seriously flawed.

What surprises me most is that Apple offers the same features for free. Why would anyone choose this app if it doesn’t provide more value?

This app has been a godsend in helping my family member to remember to take some important meds twice a day. It is also great for me as their medifriend. I no longer have to call and nag them near as often. It gives me peace of mind, to just glance at the app and see that they’ve taken their meds. The slight hiccup is that the app is not very consistent about when it will alert me that they’ve not taken their meds at the designated time. Sometimes it alerts at 45 minutes past the time, sometimes it alerts at 2 hours, but worse is when there’s no alert at all.

I don’t write reviews for apps, but after having use this app for over a year, I have to tell you this is the best app. I think I’ve ever gotten. It keeps me right on top of reminders for my medication’s and it never fails. It’s probably got every prescription and over-the-counter medication listed. I really could not live without this app.
